Fixed structural features explicitly required by the contract are allowed."},"candidate_prose":"The lower path curved beneath the end of the footbridge, bringing Deniz and Ece level with the outside of the railing. Above them, Deniz’s kite trembled against the bars whenever the wind tugged at it.

“We could have been up there already,” Deniz muttered.

“And you would still be on the wrong side of the railing,” Ece said. She held her scarf by both ends. “Wait for the wind to ease.”

Deniz frowned, but he stayed beside her.

When the next gust faded, Ece stretched up and slid the middle of her scarf beneath one corner of the kite. Deniz watched as she gently raised both ends. The scarf cradled the kite and lifted it away from the railing without tearing it.

“Now,” she said.

Deniz reached over from the safe edge of the path. The wind gave one last playful puff, but Ece kept the scarf steady. Deniz caught the kite with both hands and pulled it against his chest.

Ece saw that it was secure before lowering her scarf. She gathered it back into her hands and grinned. “Still intact.”

Deniz inspected his kite. It was the same kite, unharmed, and nobody had climbed or jumped for it.

“All right,” he said, a little reluctantly. Then he looked at Ece. “Your idea worked. Thanks for helping me get it back.”

“You’re welcome,” she said, without making a fuss.

Together they returned to the hill path. Deniz carried his recovered kite, while Ece kept hold of her scarf as the strong wind hurried them along.","deterministic_findings":[]}
